title: Remapping bluetooth headphone buttons cause win, shift, ctrl etc keys to stick / lock
author: xlm13x

status.label: One-shot remap can retain target modifiers
status.detail: Current main keeps target shortcut modifiers down after the source action key is released, until another unrelated event. That behavior matches the reported stuck Win key; related issue #19628 has newer Bluetooth media-key reports.

next_action: Reproduce the Bluetooth Play/Pause-to-Win+R case on a current build and design a targeted release path for one-shot media-key shortcut remaps.

judgment.rationale: Current main explicitly leaves target modifiers held after the source action key is released for a non-chord shortcut remap, releasing them only on a later unrelated key event. The report says a Bluetooth Play/Pause-to-Win+R mapping leaves Win held, and the linked historical issue has newer reports of Bluetooth media-key remaps leaving Ctrl, Alt, and Shift engaged. This is a plausible, source-backed root cause that should be verified before changing the intentional modifier-lifetime behavior.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.78.0 and says mapping a Bluetooth headset Play/Pause button to Win+R opens Run but leaves Win active; pressing E then triggers Win+E. The reporter reproduced it on two machines and in both admin and user modes.

The reporter linked #19628 as a similar Bluetooth media-key modifier-stuck issue. That thread has later reports on v0.94.2 and in August 2026 of Play/Pause mappings leaving Ctrl, Alt, and Shift engaged.

At upstream main 0b1dd814878f0dfbb07787d9c3e52a2897b6f769, KeyboardEventHandlers.cpp:1113-1120 documents that for a non-chord shortcut remap, the target action key is released while target modifiers are kept down until a later unrelated key event.
No linked pull request or fix covering either report was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce with a current build and design a one-shot media-key path that balances target modifier state at the source-key release without regressing remaps that intentionally preserve held modifiers.

fix_assessment.rationale: The current handler's documented deferred modifier release matches the stuck-modifier symptom, and later reports in the related issue support continued impact. A current-build reproduction must confirm that this one-shot path is responsible before implementation.

proposed_fixes.title: Balance target modifiers after one-shot media-key shortcuts
proposed_fixes.root_cause: For a non-chord shortcut remap, the current handler sends key-up for the target action key but deliberately keeps target modifiers down until a later unrelated input event. A Bluetooth media-key remap to Win+R can therefore leave Win active or let a subsequent key be interpreted with the stale modifier state.
plan: Reproduce Play/Pause-to-Win+R on a current build and compare with the Play/Pause-to-Ctrl+F10 or Alt+Shift+A cases reported in related issue #19628.
Trace the source media-key down/up events and the target shortcut's injected modifier/action events, confirming when the target modifier is released.

Adjust the one-shot remap state so target modifiers are released when the source media key is released, while preserving any intentional hold behavior for remaps whose source key remains physically down.
Add regression tests for Bluetooth media-key-to-Win+R and multi-modifier shortcuts; assert that a subsequent E key does not invoke Win+E and that no modifier remains logically pressed.
verification: After Play/Pause opens Run, pressing E does not launch Explorer and the on-screen keyboard shows no stuck Win modifier.
Play/Pause-to-Alt+Shift+A and the related reported modifier combinations leave no Ctrl, Alt, or Shift state stuck after the source button is released.
Existing shortcut and held-key remappings retain their intended key-down/key-up behavior.

confidence.rationale: The source explicitly defers target-modifier release and the reported symptom is a stuck target modifier, with later related reports. Current-version reproduction is still needed to verify the exact event path and preserve intended hold semantics.

issue_context.summary: Mapping a Bluetooth headset Play/Pause button to Win+R opens the Run dialog but can leave Win active, causing later keys to behave as Windows shortcuts.
known_information: The issue reports PowerToys 0.78.0 installed from GitHub and running as administrator.
The reporter maps Play/Pause to Win+R; after the Run dialog opens, Win remains stuck and pressing E launches Explorer. The reporter observed this on two machines in admin and user modes.
The reporter links #19628 as a similar closed issue; later comments there report Bluetooth media-key remaps leaving Ctrl, Alt, or Shift engaged on v0.94.2 and in August 2026.
Current main's non-chord shortcut-remap key-up branch releases the target action key but intentionally defers releasing target modifiers until another unrelated key event.
inferences: The deferred modifier-release policy may leave a target modifier active for a one-shot media-key event or may allow the next physical key to be processed while that stale modifier is active.
The exact behavior should be reproduced on a current build because the direct report is from v0.78.0 and the related current-version report is on a separate issue.
issue_context.analysis: The current handler's documented behavior provides a concrete path matching the stuck-Win symptom: it keeps target modifiers down after releasing the target action key for non-chord shortcut remaps. The related issue has later Bluetooth media-key confirmations but no linked fix or active owner. A focused reproduction and key-state trace should establish whether the deferred release is the cause and how to avoid changing intentional held-modifier behavior.
initial_investigation: Read the live issue body and both comments, including the reporter's link to #19628.
Read #19628 and its later comments; it contains the same Bluetooth media-key/stuck-modifier class with v0.94.2 and 2026 follow-up reports, but no linked pull request or fix.

information_gaps.information: Whether a current PowerToys build still leaves the target modifier down after the Bluetooth media key is released.
information_gaps.why_needed: The original report uses v0.78.0, and a current reproduction is needed to confirm that the present deferred-release branch causes the symptom.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Repeat the reported Play/Pause-to-Win+R mapping on a current build and check modifier state after the source button is released.

actions.label: Approve media-key modifier-release design
actions.note: Preserve intentional held-modifier behavior while ensuring one-shot Bluetooth media-key shortcuts do not leave their target modifier active.

reproduce.title: Check modifier release after a Bluetooth media-key shortcut
reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.94.2 or newer; record the exact build
prerequisites: Bluetooth headset with a Play/Pause media button
On-Screen Keyboard available to inspect modifier state
setup: Map the headset Play/Pause media key to Win+R.
steps: Press Play/Pause and confirm that the Run dialog opens.
Release the headset button and inspect whether Win remains active using On-Screen Keyboard.
Press E and confirm whether Explorer opens unexpectedly.
As an additional control, test a Play/Pause-to-Alt+Shift+A mapping.
reproduce.expected_result: The mapped shortcut runs, then all target modifiers return to their prior state; pressing E afterward does not invoke Win+E.
reproduce.setup_prompt: On a current Windows test machine, map a Bluetooth headset's Play/Pause button to Win+R, inspect modifier state after release, and verify that pressing E does not open Explorer.
